newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPANISH FIRST DIVISION WEEKEND FIXTURES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPANISH FIRST DIVISION WEEKEND FIXTURES.

text.p: Spanish league championship fixtures this weekend (current standings in parentheses, kickoff times GMT):
Influential Atletico midfielder Jose Luis Caminero hopes to be fit to play against his old side in a Madrid derby that could prove decisive in this season's championship race.
Celta must be on guard against an Extremadura side boosted by a draw with mighty Real Madrid and boasting a result from three of their last four away games.
Having scraped through on penalties in Thursday's cup game with Sevilla, Deportivo will hope not to pay the price of the effort against an Athletic side that have lost their way in recent games.

Hercules, brought down to earth after Monday's giant-killing win at Barcelona by a midweek cup defeat at second division Lleida, attempt to bounce back against Valladolid, who will be without injured defender Alberto Marcos.
Rayo defender Juan Ramon Muniz faces up to the team where he played for 17 years in a game Sporting manager Benito Floro desperately needs to win to hang on to his job.
Oviedo will be without the Spanish league's leading home-grown goalscorer, Oli Alvarez, injured in the midweek cup defeat at Compostela.
Currently managerless Logrones hope to make an appointment ahead of the clash with Racing, who should have newly-signed Real Madrid midfielder Dejan Petkovic fit to make his debut.

Javier Gracia is set to replace Swedish midfielder Hakan Mild in a game in which Real start as favourites against a Compostela side for whom Bulgarian striker Lyuboslav Penev rediscovered his goal touch in the cup win over Oviedo.
Dispirited Zaragoza crashed out of the cup midweek and will need to score just their third home win of the season to keep coach Victor Esparrago in his job.
Barcelona's Bobby Robson could find his job on the line if his side loses at Betis, whose squad recovered from an influenza outbreak to crush Granada in the cup on Wednesday.

New Espanyol coach Vicente Miera has newly-signed French goalkeeper Pascal Olmeta and Romanian striker Florin Raducioiu ready for the game against a Sevilla outfit still smarting from Thursday's unexpected cup exit at Deportivo Coruna.
